experiment: Raise --prefill-chunk-size from the documented default 256 to 1024 (equal to the existing --token-batch-size per-inference-step cap), so each short development prompt plus the fixed empty-thinking closed-thinking assistant prefill prefills in a single chunked-prefill pass rather than possibly spanning two 256-token chunks. Only the --prefill-chunk-size CMD flag value changes; every other Dockerfile byte, ENTRYPOINT (/llmd/llmd), the commented ENV block, --io-impl=zio, --batch-size=16, --token-batch-size=1024, --max-context-len=128000, --page-chunk-size=16, --backend=auto, --gpu-memory-fraction=0.9, --cache-memory-fraction=0.95, port 8000, --model=/models/model, weights/tokenizer/quantization/chat template, the frozen profile and golden outputs are preserved. No RUN steps; no extra weights, downloads, credentials or egress.
hypothesis: For this small serial greedy workload (6 short prompts x5 reps; max_tokens 16-96; fixed empty-thinking prefill), the closed-thinking chat template can push an effective input length past the 256 default, forcing a second chunked-prefill step and adding per-chunk kernel/sync overhead to TTFT. The prior page-chunk-size=64 trial moved neither TTFT (1.018x, CI [0.9937, 1.0530] includes 1, +1.78% < 3%) nor FTGR (0.997x), showing KV-cache paging granularity is not the lever here; --prefill-chunk-size is the documented knob that directly bounds chunked-prefill step count and is distinct from the failed page-chunk-size. Raising it to 1024 (<= the existing --token-batch-size cap, so no new per-step token/memory regime) lets every dev prompt prefill in one pass, targeting the TTFT primary metric while leaving serial single-stream decode (FTGR) untouched.
notes: Evidence-driven selection from the supplied context: candidate-failure.json shows native speculative drafter is unavailable (no assets/egress allowed) and page-chunk-size=64 passed all correctness gates but produced no significant TTFT or FTGR change, so a different documented knob is required. --prefill-chunk-size is documented in --help (default 256) and is not in the program.md preserve list (--io-impl=zio, --max-context-len=128000, --model=/models/model, port 8000). Value 1024 is chosen to equal the existing --token-batch-size, keeping prefill within the engine's existing per-inference-step token budget and guaranteeing single-pass prefill for any prompt up to 1024 tokens (well above these dev prompts), with no new memory regime and no OOM concern for such short inputs. Baseline TTFT is ~41ms across prompts and FTGR ~50-56 tok/s; this proposal targets TTFT only and expects FTGR to be roughly unchanged on a serial single-stream workload. Greedy temperature=0/top_k=1 outputs, golden-output match, finish_reason validity, streamed-chunk count vs usage.completion_tokens, and greedy self-consistency gates are unaffected because sampling, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, chat template, port and --model are unchanged; the closed-thinking profile is identical for baseline and candidate. Startup is unaffected (no extra asset load). This is a hypothesis for Root to build and measure on the actual GPU later; no measured gain is claimed here.
changed_knob: --prefill-chunk-size: 256 -> 1024 (single CMD flag value; all other Dockerfile bytes preserved, no RUN steps)
risk: Low. (1) If every dev prompt already prefills in a single 256-token chunk, the change is effectively a no-op on TTFT and FTFT/FTGR (no regression expected, just no gain) -- the same inert outcome as the page-chunk-size=64 trial. (2) Larger prefill-chunk-size raises transient activation memory for one prefill pass, but 1024 tokens is within the existing --token-batch-size cap and far below the 128000 context length and the 0.9 gpu-memory-fraction budget for these short prompts, so OOM risk is negligible. (3) No correctness/golden/greedy/startup risk: sampling, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, chat template, port and --model are unchanged; the closed-thinking profile is identical for baseline and candidate. (4) No extra weights, downloads, credentials or egress. (5) Startup stays <=1.5x (asset loading unchanged). Worst case: no measured movement, identical to the page-chunk-size=64 result, and the baseline is reselected as last-good.
